title: 90-161.Z: decisions and risks before ANG-wide use
subtitle:
Decision brief r1 (draft) for wing leadership, staff offices and NGB
12 November 2026

cards.label: decisions made by the PFM in 3 days and logged with dates (5 more rows are agent recommendations)
risks rated; 11 are red: act before the next build or before a second wing
decisions needed from leadership and staff offices before any wing besides ours uses it

asks: Name a government product owner and a backup maintainer for an ANG-wide tool (D3).
Send the public design repository and the gov-computer delivery method for security, OPSEC and ISSM review (D1, D2).
Get a legal opinion on the status of the work and its license, and one privacy assessment that every wing can reuse (D4, D5).
Approve the pilot path: build and test here, then one wing with less access installs it from the guide alone.

product.lead: 90-161.Z runs the DAFMAN 90-161 publishing process for an ANG wing: one record per action, coordination routed and tracked, format applied by code, every event logged.
product.stageKey: Stages 0-12 per DAFMAN 90-161 (legal last: 3.4, 5.1.8.2). Amber: code, not people, applies the DAFMAN format and checks each format rule.

users.does: Request an action, upload drafts, name coordinators, see status at any time.
Get the request with a due date and reminders; answer Concur, Concur with comment, Nonconcur or No comment.
Works one queue: format and check drafts, post, keep the product index, run periodic reviews.

needed.title: Decisions needed: governance (1 of 2)
needed.lead: These need the named offices. Policy references come from search summaries; each office confirms its own rule.

items.q: The public repository describes a DoD system and has not had a security and policy review
items.opts: A: submit it for review and remove environment details now. B: make it private (the gov computer then cannot read it). C: no change
items.rec: A: keeps the only delivery path open

items.q: Scripts reach the gov computer from a public site without ISSM approval
items.opts: A: written ISSM approval of the method now. B: signed scripts through an approved channel. C: stop the gov-computer scripts
items.rec: A now, B before any second wing

items.q: Who owns and supports the product when 90 wings depend on it
items.opts: A: this PFM alone. B: NGB-sponsored owner, backup maintainer, support model. C: each wing keeps its own copy
items.rec: B: removes the single point of failure

items.q: Legal status of the work (official duty or not) and its license
items.opts: A: JA opinion and a memo that assigns it as official duty, then a license. B: no action
items.rec: A: other wings cannot reuse it lawfully without it

needed.title: Decisions needed: governance (2 of 2)
needed.lead: Privacy and records questions. Each needs an answer before real data enters the lists at a second wing.

items.q: Lists hold names and work e-mails retrieved by name: is a privacy assessment needed
items.opts: A: one central assessment (DD Form 2930) all wings reuse. B: each wing does its own

items.q: GenAI.mil terms may not allow personal data; drafts carry names and contact details
items.opts: A: confirm the terms; remove personal details before extraction. B: ask for a written exception

items.q: Design records and test results sit in personal accounts
items.opts: A: keep an official copy in DoD365 and confirm the e-mail path with the CIO. B: no change
items.rec: A: federal records law requires an official copy

needed.title: Decisions needed: design (waiting on the PFM)
needed.lead: These block the next list build. Details: docs/reviews/2026-11-12-plan-audit-assumptions-gaps.md.

items.q: All wings share one Default environment; one install can overwrite another
items.opts: A: per-wing names and IDs. B: settings in lists, site address the only per-wing value. C: own environment

items.q: Members can edit settings and the audit log
items.opts: A: members read only; flows write the log. B: no change

items.q: How later flows find lists after the rename
items.opts: A: by address. B: by display title

items.q: Fallback when no one grants Send As
items.opts: A: switch in settings; send from the PFM. B: always from the PFM

items.q: Flows stop if the PFM leaves
items.opts: A: handover runbook and daily health check now. B: later

items.q: The app cannot be shared with a SharePoint group
items.opts: A: wing AD group. B: site M365 group

riskKey: Likelihood and impact: High, Medium or Low, rated by the project. They are judgment, not measurement.
IDs match Appendix A, which lists every risk and its response.
Red: act before the next build or before a second wing. Amber: plan a response. Green: accept and watch.
Governance ratings rest on policy titles not yet read in full (confidence medium). The named offices confirm them.

risks.risk: The public repository describes a DoD system and was not reviewed for public release
risks.mit: Security and policy review through wing PA; remove environment details now (D1)

risks.risk: Unsigned scripts reach the gov computer from a public site, with a manual step around download blocking; no ISSM approval
risks.mit: Written ISSM approval; signed scripts through an approved channel (D2)

risks.risk: One maintainer, no government owner, no funding or support model; a move or separation orphans every wing
risks.mit: NGB-sponsored owner, backup maintainer, support model, exit plan (D3)

risks.risk: All flows run on the PFM's personal connections; they stop when the account closes
risks.mit: Connection handover runbook, co-owners with their own connections, daily health check (P5)

risks.risk: One personal account controls the code every wing would run
risks.mit: Signed releases with hashes, two-person review, a government-controlled copy

risks.risk: Test results and design records sit in personal accounts; federal records law requires an official copy
risks.mit: Official copy in DoD365; confirm the e-mail path with the CIO (D7)

risks.risk: GenAI.mil terms may not allow personal data; drafts carry names and contact details
risks.mit: Confirm the terms; remove personal details before extraction (D6)

risks.risk: Status of the work and its license are unclear; no license file
risks.mit: JA opinion, duty memo, then a license (D4)

risks.risk: Unclear whether the DoD365 authorization covers the app or whether it must be registered
risks.mit: Ask the ISSM and CIO in writing before a second wing

risks.risk: All wings share one Default environment; one wing's install can overwrite another's
risks.mit: Settings in lists; site address the only per-wing value; test on the tenant (P1)

risks.risk: 24 choices in the design were never approved; flows would hard-code them
risks.mit: PFM confirms or removes each before flows are built

risks.risk: A tenant data-policy change can stop every wing's flows at once
risks.mit: Standard connectors only; ask to be told of policy changes; preflight check

risks.risk: Members can edit settings, mandatory coordinators and the audit log
risks.mit: Members read only on those lists; only flows write the log (P2)

risks.risk: Office-mailbox e-mail needs Send As rights that many PFMs cannot get
risks.mit: Settings switch with a fallback sender (P4)

risks.risk: Lists hold names and work e-mails; a privacy assessment may be required
risks.mit: One central assessment that wings reuse (D5)

risks.risk: SharePoint and Power Apps limits (5,000-item views, 12 lookups, delegation) break views or searches as data grows
risks.mit: Index filtered columns, lookup budget test, archive the log yearly

risks.risk: No error alerts, health check or backup beyond the recycle bin
risks.mit: Error handling that logs and alerts; scheduled export; one restore drill

risks.risk: No plan for actions already in progress at go-live; blank review dates would flood reminders
risks.mit: Migration mode with no notices; required dates on import

risks.risk: Coordinators outside the wing (NGB, state, other wings) may not open site files
risks.mit: PDF by e-mail and the PFM records the answer

risks.risk: The format route depends on Word and PowerShell on the gov computer; the route is not chosen yet
risks.mit: Renderer round 2 on the gov computer decides the route

risks.risk: Some drafts may be CUI; lists and files have no CUI marking or handling rule
risks.mit: CUI field, banner and rule; short PFM training

risks.risk: Canvas apps are not accessible by default (Section 508)
risks.mit: Accessibility checker at 0 errors, screen-reader and keyboard test, statement

risks.risk: DAFMAN 90-161 changes must reach every wing's rules; no one approves rule changes
risks.mit: Rule catalog versioned to the DAFMAN edition; named approver

risks.risk: No ANG-wide mandate for a publishing tool; uptake may be low
risks.mit: Offer as an optional tool endorsed by NGB; second-wing pilot first

risks.risk: Design work uses a commercial AI on a personal device (fake data only); policy acceptance not confirmed
risks.mit: Written approval of the fake-data-only method from the CIO

risks.risk: The update source sits on one wing's site; it breaks when that wing's PFM leaves
risks.mit: Host it with the product owner; co-owner on the site

risks.risk: Flows run in UTC; date-only values can shift a day; drill weekends not modeled
risks.mit: Time zone setting and conversion in every date step

risks.risk: Request limits and a future premium dependency with no funding
risks.mit: Standard connectors only; filter on the server

risks.risk: AI-assisted formatting could be blamed for content errors
risks.mit: Certifying and approving officials own content; human review stays in the process

sustain.title: Who keeps it running: three ways to own it

options.name: A. This PFM maintains it
options.what: One person builds, fixes and supports every wing in addition to their duties.
options.pro: Fastest; no new staff or agreement.
options.con: Bus factor of 1; support load grows with each wing; stops at a move.

options.name: B. NGB-sponsored product owner
options.what: A named government owner, a backup maintainer, a support model and change control; this PFM leads design.
options.pro: Survives moves; one rule set for all wings; formal approvals once.
options.con: Needs a sponsor and some time from two people.

options.name: C. Each wing keeps its own copy
options.what: Wings copy it once and maintain it themselves.
options.con: 90 diverging copies; DAFMAN changes reach no one; same approvals 90 times.

sustain.note: Recommendation by the project; not a decision until leadership approves.

close.title: Decisions requested
items: Name a product owner and backup maintainer, or sponsor the request to NGB (D3).
Task PA, OPSEC and the ISSM to review the repository and the delivery method (D1, D2).
Task JA and the Privacy Act Officer: legal status and license, one privacy assessment (D4-D6).
Approve the path: build and pilot here, then a second wing, then an ANG-wide offer.

method: Prepared with AI assistance (a commercial assistant on a personal device, fake data only). Three independent read-only reviews on 12 Nov 2026: design choices against the decisions log, engineering gaps, and governance. Policy items come from search summaries, not from the full texts; the offices named as deciders confirm them. Ratings are the project's judgment. The deck is built from docs/brief/brief.json by scripts/build_decision_brief.js.

notes.title: Purpose: give decision makers what they need to judge ANG-wide use. Nothing here is government data.
notes.bottomLine: 118 PFM decisions are logged with dates. 29 risks are rated; the 11 red ones need an owner. 7 decisions need leadership or staff offices.
notes.product: One record per action from appointment to periodic review. Code applies the format in stages 3 and 11.
notes.arch: Government data stays in DoD systems. Outside systems hold design and fake data only. The download path to the gov computer is risk R02.
notes.setup: Setup checks each right before it builds anything. A missing right gives the request text and the fallback, so a PFM with less access is not stuck.
notes.updates: A new version cannot be pushed into another wing's app. The app tells the PFM, and data-only updates copy rows after approval.
notes.decided: Foundations are decided and dated. The full log is in Appendix B.
notes.heat: Top-right cells are the red risks. Governance risks dominate; most engineering risks have a known fix.
notes.sustain: The main question for leadership: who owns this when many wings depend on it.
notes.roadmap: Each gate is a go/no-go point. No second wing starts before the governance reviews close.
